The suit was constructed by costume designer [[John Mollo]],<ref name="UVG" /> and it was finished in eleven weeks.<ref name="DAG">''[[Dressing a Galaxy: The Costumes of Star Wars]]''</ref> For ''Revenge of the Sith'', Costume Props Supervisor [[Ivo Coveney]] crafted a new set of armor that served a dual purpose. Not only was it designed to fit Christensen, but it provided an opportunity for the department to correct many of the flaws in the original costume, such as the asymmetry of the mask.<ref name="IIIsp">{{FilmVideo|IV}}</ref>

The design of Darth Vader's armor was influenced by the costume worn by The Lightning, a villain in the movie serial ''The Fighting Devil Dogs'', and the Japanese Samurai masks; the similarities between Vader's armor and the suit worn by Marvel Comics supervillain Doctor Doom have been noted as well, particularly by Doom's creators, Stan Lee and Jack Kirby.<ref name="TMBTM">{{WebCite|url=http://ae.miami.com/entertainment/ui/miami/movie.html;jsessionid=99E7F56555D15B9DC53D905EE6D926F6.prodapp15_ae_01?id=299413&reviewId=18039|text=Star Wars: The Men Behind the Mask|nobackup=1}}</ref>

Vader's iconic breathing noise was created by [[Ben Burtt]] breathing through a scuba mask, with a small mic in the scuba regulator.<ref name="IVac">{{Film|IV}} audio commentary</ref> He had originally recorded many different variations of the breathing noise, from raspy and [[asthma]]tic to cold and mechanical. While the more mechanized version was chosen, the more raspy noises were used in [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Return of the Jedi'']] after Vader was fatally injured by Sidious's Force lightning,<ref name="VIac">{{Film|VI}} audio commentary</ref> and shortly beforehand when Luke cut off his right arm. Originally, Vader was to sound like a walking emergency room, with him clicking and beeping whenever he was on scene. However, this proved too distracting, and it was cut down to just his breathing.<ref name="IVac" />

===The suit in canon===
[[File:Compspanels4wn.jpg|left|thumb|Vader's chest panels]]

{{Quote|As for the specific functions of each button on his chest plate, that remains a mystery.|[[Emily Shkoukani]]|<ref name="SWII">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-inside-intel-darth-vader-suit|text=''Star Wars'' Inside Intel: Darth Vader's Suit|int=Star Wars Inside Intel}}</ref>}}
The [[1995]] ''[[Star Wars Legends]]'' book, ''[[Star Wars Technical Journal]]'' includes diagrams detailing every button and function on Vader's chest and belt.<ref name="SWTJ">''[[Star Wars Technical Journal]]''</ref> The diagrams themselves represent Vader's chest plate as it was depicted in both the ''Empire Strikes Back'' and ''Return of the Jedi'' only.

One of the changes in the canonicity regarding the suit was that, by [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], Vader's left shoulder was completely artificial,<ref name="VI" /> and in 3 ABY, after encountering Luke on Bespin, he had remarked that his right shoulder had healed well. Since a bionic shoulder could not heal, Vader's right shoulder must still have consisted of his original flesh,<ref name="SOTEcom" /> though earlier on Mimban, Vader's right arm was removed from the shoulder.<ref name="SOTME">''[[Splinter of the Mind's Eye]]''</ref> However, whether this healing Vader spoke of was literal, sarcastic, or metaphorical is not known.<ref name="SOTEcom" /> Another change was that, for Vader's costume in Episode III, the costume, being completely new, was altered from the original design, though only slightly, to give it a newly machined, freshly created appearance. Several small changes to the neck length and shoulder couplings were intended to give Vader's movements a more mechanical look.<ref name="DAG" /> One more change over canon is that the chest panel of Darth Vader's attire changed slightly from Episodes III to IV,<ref name="III" /><ref name="IV" /> and from IV to [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|V]] and VI.<ref name="V" /><ref name="VI" /> The canonical reason for this has not been put forth. Also, the control panel from Episodes V and VI bore Hebrew [[Letraset]] lettering decals that one fan theorised as translating to: "His deeds will not be forgiven, until he merits."<ref name="TC1">{{WebCite|url=http://www.vaderpainter.com/faq.html|text=VaderPainter: Bringing Your Armor To Life|quote=Put together, the sentence reads - 'His deeds will not be forgiven, until he merits'&thinsp;|archivedate=20070822111123}}</ref> However, some of the letters are rotated or inverted and the translation has never been confirmed by Lucasfilm.

The suit has been referenced several times in the [[Star Wars Legends|Expanded Universe]], an example being in the ''[[Star Wars: Legacy]]'' comics, [[Cade Skywalker]] is seen to wear a pair of trousers very similar to Vader's as a part of his outfit.<ref name="LEG">''[[Star Wars: Legacy]]''</ref> As well, in ''[[Star Wars: Union]]'', while Mara was trying on wedding dresses, one of the dresses resembled Vader's armor. Leia told the designer Mara turned it down because "The bride doesn't want to dress like the father of the groom."<ref name="U">''[[Star Wars: Union]]''</ref>
In the original plot of ''[[Star Wars: Dark Empire]]'', the Empire would have an impostor wear Darth Vader's armor, or a replica of it, in order to intimidate far-flung worlds enough to submit to obedience, but George Lucas vetoed the idea.<ref name="Interview">{{WebCite|url=http://www.jazmaonline.com/interviews/interviews2007.asp?intID=432|text=Interview with Tom Veitch|author=Vasseur, Richard|date=2007-02-04|archivedate=20160311051126}}</ref>

On October 1, 2011, a guidebook was released that expanded on the construction and functions of Darth Vader's armor. According to author Daniel Wallace's blog entry "5 things you didn't know about Darth Vader," they based some elements of Darth Vader's armor (e.g., one of the ten layers of his armor) on NASA astronaut suits, which they had studied before writing the book.

===Non-canon===
[[File:WhiteVader.jpg|thumb|right|120px|Anakin Skywalker's white armor]]
In ''[[Star Wars Infinities: The Empire Strikes Back]]'', during a vision while fighting [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]], Vader's armor reverts to one of Ralph McQuarrie's original designs, but is shortly thereafter destroyed by the spirits of Obi-Wan Kenobi, [[Mace Windu/Legends|Mace Windu]] and [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]].

In ''[[Star Wars Infinities: Return of the Jedi]]'', after returning to the [[Light side of the Force/Legends|light side of the Force]], Anakin Skywalker's armor was recolored white.<ref name="I4">[[Star Wars Infinities: Return of the Jedi 4|''Star Wars Infinities: Return of the Jedi'' 4]]</ref>

In concept art for what was going to be ''Star Wars: Battlefront IV'', Vader would have received two variations of his armor, both of which were for a what-if storyline where he became the [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Galactic Emperor]]. Although both were overall similar to his standard armor, one concept drawing depicted a sleeker armor appearance with a slightly different life-support panel, as well as him wearing a cape resembling Sith robes, including a hood, while the other possessed gold linings and slightly more advanced-looking armor, with the cape having an interior red, as well a slightly circular and primarily red life-support panel.<ref>{{WebCite|url=https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2018-03-13-cancelled-star-wars-battlefield-4-art-shows-dark-side-luke-jedi-maul|text=Cancelled Star Wars Battlefront 4 art shows dark side Luke, Jedi Maul|author=Philips, Tom|date=2018-04-11|archivedate=20200510180856}}</ref>
